docs.title: Group Administrator Guide
docs.text:
Version 1.1 — Development Review

This guide is under active review. Procedures may be refined as administrator training and reviewer feedback continue.

Group Administrators manage the day-to-day work for the groups assigned to them. Depending on district policy and permissions, this usually includes:

  • maintaining the group home page;
  • viewing and managing group membership;
  • creating or cloning Accordion Agendas;
  • adding and updating agenda attachments;
  • publishing agendas and sending notifications; and
  • finding drafts and reusable templates.

docs.title: Recommended starting point
docs.text:
1. Review the Group home page.
  2. Confirm the correct group members.
  3. Use Drafts & Templates to clone an existing agenda whenever possible.
  4. Review the Best practices before publishing or revising an agenda.
  5. Use the FAQ when content or an agenda appears to be missing.

Questions are encouraged

Ask for help whenever you are unsure. There are no stupid questions, and a quick question is often safer than trying to undo an avoidable change.

docs.title: Add a group member
docs.text: Add only an existing schoolboard.net account that has been approved for the group.

docs.title: Add the membership
docs.text:
1. Open the correct group and select Members.
  2. Select Add member.
  3. Begin entering the username in User.
  4. Select the correct result from the autocomplete list.
  5. Leave URL alias empty unless the district has given specific instructions.
  6. Do not assign additional roles unless a District Administrator has approved them.
  7. Select Save.
  8. Return to the Members list and verify the username.

Figure SB-DST-016. Add an existing user to the group.

User not found

If autocomplete does not find the user, do not create a substitute account or select a similar name. Ask a District Administrator to confirm or create the account.

docs.title: Create agendas and add attachments
docs.text: A Group Administrator may create and update agendas for an assigned group and add the approved files that support each agenda item. District Administrators can perform the same agenda actions.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
• Confirm that you are working in the correct group.
  • Confirm the meeting title, date, time, and publication status.
  • Use only approved public or restricted attachments.
  • Confirm the intended access level before publishing an attachment.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
1. Open the assigned group and begin a new agenda or open the approved agenda draft.
  2. Enter or verify the meeting details.
  3. Add agenda sections and items in the approved order.
  4. Add each attachment to the correct agenda item.
  5. Confirm the attachment title and access setting.
  6. Preview the agenda.
  7. Open each attachment from the preview to confirm that it works.
  8. Save or publish according to district procedure.

Complete how-to

Use the Accordion Agenda Guide for screenshots and detailed instructions covering agenda creation, sections, expandable content, attachments, ordering, preview, revisions, notifications, and publishing.

docs.title: Before publishing
docs.text:
• Confirm the correct group and meeting.
  • Confirm that agenda sections are in the intended order.
  • Confirm that each attachment is attached to the correct item.
  • Confirm that public and restricted materials have the correct access setting.
  • Preview the agenda and open every attachment.

Protect restricted material

Do not publish an attachment until its access setting has been verified. If you are uncertain whether a file should be public, stop and confirm with the District Administrator or other designated district approver.

docs.title: Group Administrator Best Practices
docs.text: These practices help districts maintain consistent agendas, reduce accidental changes, and simplify support.

docs.title: Designate one primary agenda owner
docs.text:
During implementation, designate one person as the primary owner of each meeting agenda. That person should normally:

  • clone the correct template;
  • update the agenda;
  • coordinate attachments;
  • review the finished agenda; and
  • publish and send notifications.

Other Group Administrators may add or update attachments as they are trained, but changes to the overall agenda structure should initially remain with the primary administrator.

Tip

Avoid having multiple administrators edit the same agenda at the same time.

docs.title: Clone templates whenever possible
docs.text:
Use Drafts & Templates as the normal starting point. Build a new agenda from Add Content only when an appropriate template does not exist.

Templates help preserve recurring agenda sections, standard language, approved formatting, recurring attachments, and a consistent public experience.

docs.title: Verify the assigned group
docs.text:
Every agenda must be assigned to the correct group. An agenda that is unassigned or assigned to the wrong group may appear to be missing from the expected group page.

Before publishing, verify the meeting title, assigned group, meeting date and time, visibility, publication status, and notification selections.

docs.title: Notify the group about revisions without notifying the public
docs.text:
Use this procedure only after the agenda has already been published and the original group and public notifications have been sent.

  1. Open the published agenda for editing.
  2. Make the required changes.
  3. Enter a clear description in the Revision information field.
  4. Change Visibility to Private.
  5. Select Notifications.
  6. Click Save. The notification is sent to members of the assigned group.
  7. Immediately reopen the agenda.
  8. Change Visibility back to Public.
  9. Clear Notifications.
  10. Click Save again.

The agenda is public again, and no additional public notification is sent.

Do not leave the agenda private

Complete the second save immediately. Until visibility is returned to Public, the public cannot view the agenda.

docs.title: Write useful revision descriptions
docs.text:
Use descriptions that tell board members exactly what changed, such as:

  • Added Finance Committee report
  • Replaced Attachment C
  • Corrected meeting start time
  • Added Executive Session item

Minor spelling or formatting corrections may not require another notification. Follow district practice.

docs.title: Preview before publishing
docs.text: Before publication, review the agenda as a board member or public visitor would see it. Confirm that headings and sections are in the expected order, attachments open correctly, links are descriptive, visibility is correct, and notification settings match the intended audience.

docs.title: Ask before guessing
docs.text: When a step or setting is unclear, pause and ask. There are no stupid questions. A quick support question is preferable to recreating content or sending an unintended notification.

docs.title: I cannot find an agenda in the group
docs.text:
First check Drafts & Templates. The agenda may still be unpublished.

Also confirm that the agenda was assigned to the correct group. Content assigned to another group will not appear where expected.

If the agenda still cannot be found, ask a District Administrator to search the site-wide Content list.

docs.title: I see several entries with the same agenda title
docs.text:
The site may be displaying revisions. Review the Updated date and time and open the most recent entry.

Do not delete older entries until you have confirmed which entry is the current published agenda.

docs.title: Should I create an agenda from Add Content or clone a template?
docs.text: Clone a template from Drafts & Templates whenever a suitable template exists. Use Add Content only when the agenda must be created from scratch.

docs.title: Why is a published agenda missing from the public group page?
docs.text:
Check all of the following:

  • Visibility is set to Public.
  • The agenda is Published.
  • The correct Group is assigned.
  • The meeting date and other required fields are complete.

docs.title: How do I notify only group members about a revision?
docs.text: Follow the procedure in Notify the group about revisions without notifying the public.

docs.title: Can several administrators edit one agenda?
docs.text: They may have permission to do so, but one person should own the agenda preparation process. Avoid simultaneous editing and coordinate attachment updates.

docs.title: What should I do when I am unsure?
docs.text: Stop and ask. There are no stupid questions. Contact the district's primary administrator or schoolboard.net support before making a change that might affect publication, visibility, notifications, or agenda structure.

docs.title: Understand the Group Home Page
docs.text: When you are signed in as a Group or District Administrator, the group home page provides the main tools for managing that group.

docs.title: Main administrator tools
docs.text:
1. Edit Update the content displayed on the group home page.

  2. Members View and manage the users assigned to the group.

  3. Add Content Create new group content, including an Accordion Agenda built from scratch.

  4. Drafts & Templates Open unpublished content and reusable agenda templates.

docs.title: Preferred way to create an Accordion Agenda
docs.text: Most agendas should be created by cloning a template.

docs.title: Preferred method: Drafts & Templates
docs.text: Open Drafts & Templates, locate the appropriate meeting template, and clone it. This preserves recurring sections, formatting, and standard content.

docs.title: Alternative: Add Content
docs.text:
Use Add Content when no suitable template exists and the agenda must be built from scratch.

Best practice

Use templates for recurring meeting types. Consistent templates reduce preparation time and help prevent accidental changes to the agenda structure.

docs.title: Edit the group home page
docs.text:
Select Edit on the group home page to update the public information for the group.

Review the title, body text, and optional group footer before saving. Create a new revision when the district wants a record of the change.

Warning

The group title and basic page structure should remain consistent unless the district has approved a change.

docs.title: Terms
docs.text:
User account The person's schoolboard.net sign-in identity. District Administrators manage accounts.

Group membership The connection that gives an existing user access to a specific group.

Group Administrator A user authorized to manage membership in an assigned group.

District Administrator A user authorized to manage district-wide accounts, roles, groups, and access.

docs.title: Current review scope
docs.text:
This review draft documents viewing, adding, and removing group members. It also identifies the Group Administrator's authority to create agendas and add agenda attachments for an assigned group.

The detailed creation and publishing procedure is maintained in the separate Accordion Agenda Guide, shared by Group Administrators and District Administrators. This guide does not document account creation, group creation or editing, district roles, or account blocking.

docs.title: Screenshot reuse
docs.text: Figures SB-DST-014, SB-DST-016, SB-DST-017, and SB-DST-020 are reused from the District Administrator screenshot set because the membership interface and actions are the same.

docs.title: Remove a group member
docs.text: Removing membership affects only the selected group. It does not block, cancel, or delete the user account.

docs.title: Open the membership operation
docs.text:
1. Open the correct group's Members tab.
  2. Find the exact username.
  3. Open the member's Operations menu.
  4. Select Remove member.

Figure SB-DST-017. Open the membership Operations menu.

Edit member is outside this role

The shared Operations menu may display Edit member. This guide authorizes Group Administrators to add and remove membership only. Contact a District Administrator when a membership role must be changed.

docs.title: Confirm removal
docs.text:
1. Read the confirmation and verify the user and group.
  2. Select Delete to remove the membership.
  3. Select Cancel if anything is incorrect or uncertain.
  4. Return to the Members list and verify that the membership is gone.

Figure SB-DST-020. Confirm or cancel removal of the group membership.

Do not continue if uncertain

If the username or group is not the one you intended, select Cancel and start again.

docs.text:

docs.title: The user does not appear in autocomplete
docs.text:
• Confirm the spelling of the username.
  • Confirm that the person already has a schoolboard.net account.
  • Contact a District Administrator if the account is missing or blocked.

docs.title: The user still cannot see group materials
docs.text:
• Confirm that the correct group was changed.
  • Confirm that the username appears in the Members list.
  • Ask the user to sign out and sign in again.
  • Contact a District Administrator if access remains incorrect.

docs.title: The wrong membership was removed
docs.text: Return to Add member and restore the correct existing user. Notify the District Administrator if the change affected access during an active meeting or review period.

docs.title: An operation is not available
docs.text: Do not try to work around missing permissions. Confirm that you are in the assigned group and contact a District Administrator.

docs.title: Safety checklist
docs.text:
• Use only the access assigned to you.
  • Verify the group and username before saving.
  • Avoid changing unfamiliar roles or URL aliases.
  • Never share administrator credentials.
  • Sign out on shared devices.

docs.title: What Group Administrators can do
docs.text: A Group Administrator manages membership and meeting agenda content in an assigned group.

docs.title: Included in this guide
docs.text:
• View the group's current members.
  • Add an existing user to the group.
  • Remove a user from the group.
  • Verify that a membership change was completed.
  • Create and update agendas for the assigned group.
  • Add approved agenda attachments and confirm that they open correctly.

docs.title: Contact a District Administrator for
docs.text:
• Creating a user account.
  • Changing a username, email address, or password.
  • Assigning district-level roles or permissions.
  • Creating, renaming, or changing the type of a group.
  • Blocking, restoring, or cancelling a user account.
  • Resolving access that remains incorrect after the group membership is verified.

Membership is not the user account

Removing someone from a group does not block or delete the person's schoolboard.net account. It removes only that group membership.

Use the shared agenda instructions

Agenda creation is available to both Group Administrators and District Administrators. Follow the Accordion Agenda Guide for the full creation, section, attachment, preview, and publishing workflow.

docs.title: View group members
docs.text:
Open the assigned group and select Members. The list identifies each user, any group membership role, the update and join dates, and available operations.

Figure SB-DST-014. Review the current group membership list.

docs.title: Before changing membership
docs.text:
1. Confirm the group name in the page heading or breadcrumb.
  2. Look for the username in the existing Members list.
  3. Do not add the same user twice.
  4. If the username is unfamiliar or ambiguous, stop and confirm the correct account.
